template_comparison.canonical_problem:
Consider the Lotka-Volterra model above, where $x=x(t)$ represents the predators and $y=y(t)$ represents the prey.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′} &=-0.4x+0.4xy \\ {y}^{′} &=y-4xy\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Evaluate the Jacobian of the system at the equilibrium point $\mathbf{x^\ast}=[0.25, \, 1]^T,$ and classify this equilibrium point.
template_comparison.canonical_solution:
Let's denote $f_1(x,y)=-0.4x+0.4xy$ and $f_2(x,y)=y-4xy.$

Now, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-0.4x+0.4xy)=-0.4+0.4y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-0.4x+0.4xy)=0.4x \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-4xy)=-4y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y-4xy)=1-4x\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the Jacobian matrix is
$$
J
=
{\left[ \begin{array}{cc}- 0.4 + 0.4 y & 0.4 x \\ - 4 y & 1 - 4 x\end{array} \right]}.
$$

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium $\mathbf{x}^\ast = {\left[ \begin{array}{c}0.25 \\ 1\end{array} \right]}$ to get

$$
J(\mathbf{x}^\ast)
=
{\left[ \begin{array}{cc}- 0.4 + 0.4 ( 1 ) & 0.4 ( 0.25 ) \\ - 4 ( 1 ) & 1 - 4 ( 0.25 )\end{array} \right]}
=
{\left[ \begin{array}{cc}\bbox[4pt,border:1pt solid gainsboro]{0} & \bbox[4pt,border:1pt solid gainsboro]{0.1} \\ \bbox[4pt,border:1pt solid gainsboro]{- 4} & \bbox[4pt,border:1pt solid gainsboro]{0}\end{array} \right]}.
$$

To find the eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix, we write down the characteristic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{vmatrix}-\lambda  & 0.1 \\ -4 & -\lambda \end{vmatrix} & =0 \\ (-\lambda )(-\lambda )-(-4)\cdot 0.1 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+0.4 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation, we get the eigenvalues $\lambda_{1,2} = \pm 0.2\sqrt{10}\,\text{i}.$ Since the eigenvalues are purely imaginary, our equilibrium is a stable center.

**Note:**
For the Lotka-Volterra model (as in this problem), it is safe to classify the nonzero equilibrium as a center when the linearization has purely imaginary eigenvalues. 

**Watch out!** 
In contrast, for a general nonlinear system, the Jacobian test alone is inconclusive (additional analysis is required to determine whether the equilibrium is a true center or a spiral sink/source).

Let's denote ${f}_{1}(x,y)=2x-3xy$ and ${f}_{2}(x,y)=-5y+4xy.$

Now, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x-3xy)=2-3y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x-3xy)=-3x \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-5y+4xy)=4y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-5y+4xy)=-5+4x\end{aligned}
$$

$$
J=\begin{bmatrix}2-3y & -3x \\ 4y & -5+4x\end{bmatrix}.
$$

$$
J({x}^{∗})=\begin{bmatrix}2-3(0) & -3(0) \\ 4(0) & -5+4(0)\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -5\end{bmatrix}.

questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote $f_1(x,y)=x-0.5xy$ and $f_2(x,y)=-0.2y+2xy.$

Now, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial f_1}{\partial x}&=1-0.5y, & \frac{\partial f_1}{\partial y}&=-0.5x, \\ \frac{\partial f_2}{\partial x}&=2y, & \frac{\partial f_2}{\partial y}&=-0.2+2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the Jacobian matrix is

$$
J(x,y)=\begin{bmatrix}1-0.5y & -0.5x \\ 2y & -0.2+2x\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium $\mathbf{x}^{\ast}=\begin{bmatrix}0.1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}$ to get

$$
J(\mathbf{x}^{\ast})=\begin{bmatrix}1-0.5(2) & -0.5(0.1) \\ 2(2) & -0.2+2(0.1)\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0 & -0.05 \\ 4 & 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$

To find the eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix, we write down the characteristic equation:

$$
\det(J(\mathbf{x}^{\ast})-\lambda I)=\lambda^2+0.2=0.
$$

The eigenvalues are $\lambda_{1,2}=\pm\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\,\mathrm{i}.$ For this classical Lotka–Volterra model, the positive coexistence equilibrium is a stable center. It is not asymptotically stable.

Consider the Lotka-Volterra model with carrying capacity below, where $x=x(t)$ represents the prey and $y=y(t)$ represents the predators.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′} &=5x(1-x)-xy \\ {y}^{′} &=-y+2xy\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Evaluate the Jacobian of the system at the equilibrium point $\mathbf{x^\ast}=[0.5, \, 2.5]^T,$ and classify this equilibrium point.
template_comparison.canonical_solution:
Let's denote $f_1(x,y)=5x(1-x)-xy$ and $f_2(x,y)=-y+2xy.$

Now, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(5x(1-x)-xy)=5-10x-y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(5x(1-x)-xy)=-x \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-y+2xy)=2y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-y+2xy)=-1+2x\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the Jacobian matrix is
$$
J
=
{\left[ \begin{array}{cc}5 - 10 x - y & - x \\ 2 y & - 1 + 2 x\end{array} \right]}.
$$

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium $\mathbf{x}^\ast = {\left[ \begin{array}{c}0.5 \\ 2.5\end{array} \right]}$ to get

$$
J(\mathbf{x}^\ast)
=
{\left[ \begin{array}{cc}5 - 10 ( 0.5 ) - 2.5 & - 0.5 \\ 2 ( 2.5 ) & - 1 + 2 ( 0.5 )\end{array} \right]}
=
{\left[ \begin{array}{cc}\bbox[4pt,border:1pt solid gainsboro]{- 2.5} & \bbox[4pt,border:1pt solid gainsboro]{- 0.5} \\ \bbox[4pt,border:1pt solid gainsboro]{5} & \bbox[4pt,border:1pt solid gainsboro]{0}\end{array} \right]}.
$$

To find the eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix, we write down the characteristic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{vmatrix}-2.5-\lambda  & -0.5 \\ 5 & -\lambda \end{vmatrix} & =0 \\ (-2.5-\lambda )(-\lambda )-5(-0.5) & =0 \\ \lambda (2.5+\lambda )+2.5 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+2.5\lambda +2.5 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation, we get the eigenvalues $\lambda_{1,2} = -1.25 \pm 0.25\sqrt{15}\,\text{i}.$ Since the eigenvalues are complex with negative real parts, our equilibrium is an asymptotically stable spiral sink.

$$

\mathbf{u}^{\prime}=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ -3 & 0\end{bmatrix}\mathbf{u},
$$

where the deviation vector is

$$
\mathbf{u}=\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{x}^{\ast}=\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}x-1 \\ y-2\end{bmatrix}.
$$
